backlog.spec: In fit_predict, change the SVR hyperparameters from C=5.0, epsilon=0.05 to C=2.0, epsilon=0.1 (a smaller C gives more regularization). Keep everything else unchanged. If it helps, a follow-up can try C=10.
backlog.title: Tune SVR C and epsilon

backlog.spec: In featurize and descriptors, parse each SMILES, keep only the largest fragment using rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags(asMols=True) choosing the one with most heavy atoms, then compute fingerprints and descriptors on it. Use a shared helper function get_mol(s).
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest-fragment canonicalization

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform rank target with a normal-score target. Compute r = (rankdata(y) - 0.5)/len(y) as now, then map it through scipy.stats.norm.ppf to obtain a roughly Gaussian target. Standardize it with mean and std as in the current code (mu, sd from the training targets), fit the SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5.0, epsilon=0.05) on the standardized values, and return model.predict(K_test). The kernel and everything else are unchanged. Since Spearman depends only on ranks, the extra tail stretching changes the fit only through the loss weighting of the SVR tube.
backlog.title: Probit (normal-score) rank target

backlog.spec: Change gamma = 1.0 / D.shape[1] to gamma = 0.5 / D.shape[1] so the descriptor RBF kernel is smoother. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Descriptor RBF gamma scaling

backlog.spec: Two earlier changes each gave a borderline gain on their own but were never tried together; combine them in one script. First, add a Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprint kernel: build the pharmacophore fingerprint with rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D (Generate.Gen2DFingerprint with the Gobbi_Pharm2D factory), fold it to 4096 bits with a simple modulo hash into a 0/1 numpy array, compute its Tanimoto kernel, and average it equally with the existing Morgan-Tanimoto kernel and the descriptor RBF kernel so the mix is (1/3, 1/3, 1/3). Second, before fitting the SVR, fit a Ridge(alpha=10) on seven standardized physchem descriptors (MolWt, MolLogP, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, RingCount) to the rank-normalized target, subtract its in-sample prediction from the target, fit the SVR on that residual, and add the ridge prediction back on the test molecules. Keep everything else (rank target, C=5, epsilon=0.05) unchanged.
backlog.title: Combine the pharmacophore kernel with the physchem ridge prior

backlog.spec: Compute Gasteiger partial charges with rdkit.Chem.rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges(mol) for each molecule. From the per-atom values of the heavy atoms, build a 6-element feature vector: counts of atoms with charge below -0.25, between -0.25 and -0.05, between -0.05 and 0.05, between 0.05 and 0.25, above 0.25, and the maximum absolute charge. Replace NaN charges by 0. Append these 6 columns to the standardized RDKit descriptor matrix D before the descriptor RBF kernel is built (standardize and clip them the same way). Gamma stays 1/n_descriptors computed on the enlarged matrix. The rest of the pipeline is unchanged.
backlog.title: Gasteiger partial-charge histogram descriptors

backlog.spec: Keep the current kernel SVR exactly as is, and add a second, structurally different model: a LightGBM regressor (objective='regression', learning_rate=0.03, n_estimators=600, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=10, feature_fraction=0.5, bagging_fraction=0.8, bagging_freq=1, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1) trained on the concatenation of the 2048 Morgan bits and the standardized clipped RDKit descriptors against the same rank-normalized target. Convert each model's test predictions to ranks with scipy.stats.rankdata and return 0.7 * rank(SVR) + 0.3 * rank(LightGBM), rescaled by dividing by the number of test molecules. Tree ensembles and kernel methods make different errors, and rank averaging is the natural combiner for a Spearman loss.
backlog.title: Rank-average blend of the kernel SVR with LightGBM

backlog.spec: Compute atom-pair fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048) as binary vectors. Compute a Tanimoto kernel on them. Average it with the existing kernels (three-way mean: Morgan, atom pair, descriptor RBF).
backlog.title: Add atom-pair and topological-torsion fingerprint kernels

backlog.spec: Before fitting the SVR, replace each training target with a shrunken version: for each training molecule, average the rank targets of its k=5 nearest training neighbors under the Tanimoto similarity (excluding itself), and blend 0.8 * own rank + 0.2 * neighbor mean. Fit the SVR on these smoothed targets and predict the test set as before. The smoothing dampens label noise between near analogs, which is common in clearance assays. Keep k and the blend weight as module-level constants.
backlog.title: Scaffold-stratified target smoothing via a kNN prior on the Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Hepatocyte clearance is driven largely by lipophilicity moderated by size, polarity and ionization, and those interactions are multiplicative rather than additive, which a plain RBF kernel on raw descriptors represents poorly. Before the existing standardize-and-clip step, append a small block of explicitly constructed cross terms computed from RDKit descriptors: MolLogP*MolLogP, MolLogP*TPSA, MolLogP/(1+NumRotatableBonds), MolLogP - 0.01*MolWt (a crude ligand-efficiency-like term), TPSA/MolWt, NumAromaticRings*MolLogP, and FractionCSP3*MolLogP. Guard every division with a small epsilon and nan_to_num the block. Standardize and clip the extended matrix exactly as the current code does, and update gamma to 1.0 / (number of kept columns). Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Lipophilicity interaction features for the descriptor kernel

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a small grid over C in {1, 5, 20} and epsilon in {0.02, 0.05, 0.1} using 4-fold KFold on the training data only (shuffle=True, random_state=seed). Each candidate reuses the precomputed training kernel, sliced by index, so the cost is small. Score each candidate by Spearman between out-of-fold predictions and the true values, refit the SVR with the best (C, epsilon) on all training data, and predict the test set. Do not look at the test fold during tuning.
backlog.title: Tune the SVR C and epsilon with inner cross-validation

backlog.spec: Fit the current kernel SVR as it stands, then learn what it systematically misses. Inside fit_predict, run a 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed) over the training molecules to get out-of-fold SVR predictions (refitting the same precomputed-kernel SVR on each inner training subset, slicing the already-computed train-train kernel). Compute the residual r = y_rank_normalized - oof_prediction, fit a small LightGBM model (learning_rate=0.05, n_estimators=300, num_leaves=7, min_child_samples=20, random_state=seed, verbose=-1) on the standardized RDKit descriptors to predict r, and return full_svr_prediction + 0.5 * residual_model_prediction(test descriptors). The 0.5 shrinkage keeps the correction conservative. The inner CV only re-solves a 776-row precomputed-kernel SVR five times, which is cheap.
backlog.title: LightGBM residual correction on out-of-fold SVR residuals

backlog.spec: After dropping constant descriptors and before standardizing, remove descriptors that have absolute Pearson correlation above 0.95 with an earlier kept column (computed on training data only; apply the same column mask to test). Then gamma = 1/number of remaining columns.
backlog.title: Descriptor correlation pruning

backlog.spec: Swap sklearn.svm.SVR for sklearn.svm.NuSVR with kernel='precomputed', nu=0.5, C=5.0, leaving the kernel construction and rank-normalized target untouched. NuSVR directly controls the fraction of support vectors rather than a fixed epsilon tube, which adapts the tube width to the spread of the rank-normalized target instead of fixing it at 0.05. If it helps, it is a one-line change with no extra cost; the run time should be essentially identical to the current script.
backlog.title: NuSVR head in place of epsilon-SVR

backlog.spec: Compute a local density for each training molecule as the number of other training molecules whose combined kernel value K_train[i, j] exceeds 0.6 (excluding the diagonal), then set weight w_i = 1/(1 + density_i/median(density)). Normalize the weights to mean 1. Pass them through SVR.fit(K_train, y_std, sample_weight=w) so that molecules in crowded regions of chemical space (many near-analogues) contribute less to the fit. Use the same C=5.0 and epsilon=0.05, same kernel and same rank target. This is different from scaffold-frequency weighting because it uses the kernel similarity itself.
backlog.title: Density-based sample weights for the SVR

backlog.spec: Change the descriptor RBF gamma from 1/n_features to 0.5/n_features. Also reduce the clip range of the standardized descriptors from 5 to 3 to limit outliers. Test both changes together.
backlog.title: RBF gamma tuning

backlog.spec: Add RDKit's ErG pharmacophore-style fingerprint: from rdkit.Chem import rdReducedGraphs, call rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint(mol) for each molecule (train and test), giving a real-valued vector of length 315. Standardize it using the training mean and std (std floor 1e-9, clip to [-5, 5]). Build an RBF kernel on the standardized ErG vectors with gamma = 1/315 and use the mean of three kernels: K = (1/3)*(tanimoto_morgan + rbf_descriptors + rbf_erg). Keep the SVR C=5.0, epsilon=0.05 and the rank-normalized target unchanged.
backlog.title: Extended reduced-graph (ErG) fingerprint kernel

backlog.spec: Build a two-model ensemble inside fit_predict and average their predictions after converting each to ranks. Model A is exactly the current kernel SVR. Model B is a LightGBM regressor (n_estimators=700, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=10, feature_fraction=0.4, bagging_fraction=0.8, bagging_freq=1, lambda_l2=5.0, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed, verbose=-1) trained on the concatenation of the 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint and the standardised RDKit descriptor block, with the same rank-transformed target. Final prediction = 0.5*rankdata(pred_A)/n + 0.5*rankdata(pred_B)/n. Since the metric is Spearman, averaging ranks rather than raw values is the right pooling and makes the two models' scales irrelevant. Rationale: a smooth similarity-based model and an axis-aligned tree model make largely decorrelated errors on scaffold-split data, so their rank average usually beats either alone.
backlog.title: Rank-average ensemble of SVR and gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Make the structural kernel an average over several independent fingerprint views instead of one. For b in {1024, 2048, 4096} and radius in {2, 3}, build the Morgan fingerprint, compute its Tanimoto matrix, and average all six matrices into K_struct; different hash sizes collide different substructure pairs, so averaging cancels a chunk of the folding noise that a single 2048-bit fingerprint bakes in. Combine with the descriptor RBF kernel as before (0.5/0.5) and leave the SVR unchanged. This is pure variance reduction on the kernel itself, costs a few seconds, and adds no hyperparameters. Rationale: hash collisions in a folded fingerprint act like random feature corruption; ensembling over fold sizes and radii is the cheapest available antidote.
backlog.title: Fingerprint bagging over seeds and bit sizes

backlog.spec: Besides the SVR, fit sklearn KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.5) on the same kernel and standardized target. Return the average of the rank-normalized predictions (rankdata) of the SVR and KernelRidge.
backlog.title: Add GP-style kernel ridge ensemble member

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM on the rank target with learning_rate=0.05 and up to 2000 trees. Hold out a stratified 15% of the training fold as validation (split by rank bins, random_state=seed). Use early_stopping(100) on the validation Spearman via a custom eval metric, or on l2 loss if simpler. Then refit on the full training fold with the best iteration count scaled by 1/0.85. This replaces the fixed N_TREES with a data-driven stopping point, which is the main regularizer for boosted trees here.
backlog.title: Learning-rate and tree-count schedule with early stopping on inner validation

backlog.spec: Compute the heavy-atom count for every training and test molecule (m.GetNumHeavyAtoms()). Split the training set into three groups by its tertiles (cut points from the training data only). For each test molecule, assign it to the group of its size tertile and predict with an SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5.0, epsilon=0.05) trained only on that group's training molecules, using the usual kernel K = 0.5*(tanimoto + rbf) and rank-normalized target standardized as before. Each group needs its own kernel submatrix (index selection on K_train). If a group has fewer than 30 molecules, fall back to the global SVR for that group.
backlog.title: Heavy-atom-size tertile specialist SVRs

backlog.spec: The RDKit descriptor block is highly redundant (many descriptors are near-duplicates), so the Euclidean distance that feeds the RBF kernel is dominated by whichever descriptor family happens to have the most members. After the existing standardize-and-clip step, fit sklearn.decomposition.PCA(n_components=50, whiten=True, random_state=seed) on the training descriptor matrix, transform both train and test, and build the RBF kernel on the whitened 50-dimensional scores with gamma = 1.0 / 50. Everything else (Morgan-Tanimoto kernel, 0.5/0.5 mix, rank target, SVR settings) is unchanged.
backlog.title: PCA-whitened descriptors before the RBF kernel

backlog.spec: Train 5 LightGBM regressors on the descriptors plus Morgan bits, each with a different seed derived from the seed argument (seed + k for k in 0..4). Use subsample=0.7 with subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.3, learning_rate=0.03, and num_leaves=15, and set n_estimators to 400. Average the five predictions on the rank target. Bagging over row and column subsamples lowers variance on a dataset of about 800 training molecules, and the seed argument stays the only source of randomness.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged LightGBM with row and column subsampling

backlog.spec: Append to the descriptor matrix D (before standardization) log1p of heavy atom count, number of rotatable bonds, and fraction of sp3 carbons duplicated once more as extra columns, effectively upweighting size/flexibility in the RBF kernel. Use Descriptors.HeavyAtomCount, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3 for train and test.
backlog.title: Add 3D-free shape/size count features to descriptor kernel

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5.0, epsilon=0.05) with sklearn NuSVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5.0, nu=0.5). Keep the same kernel K_train = 0.5*(tanimoto + rbf), the same rank-normalized target and the same standardization of the target (y-mu)/sd before fitting. Predictions are returned unchanged with model.predict(K_test). Nu controls the fraction of support vectors, so nu replaces epsilon as the sparsity knob. Use nu=0.5 as the only setting in this job, with C=5.0 left as is.
backlog.title: NuSVR head instead of epsilon-SVR

backlog.spec: Add a second Tanimoto kernel from count-free binary FCFP (GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen, radius 3, 2048 bits). Average three kernels equally: ECFP Tanimoto, FCFP Tanimoto and descriptor RBF.
backlog.title: Larger radius and feature-based Morgan added to the kernel

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 0.5 weight in K = w * Tanimoto + (1 - w) * RBF with a choice of w from {0.25, 0.5, 0.75}. For each w, run inner 4-fold CV on the training fold with the existing SVR settings and measure Spearman of the out-of-fold predictions. Refit with the best w on the full training fold and predict the test set. Compute the descriptor-RBF kernel once and reuse it across the sweep, because only the mixing changes between candidates.
backlog.title: Mixing-weight sweep for the combined kernel

backlog.spec: In featurize(), call Chem.AddHs(mol) on each parsed molecule before computing the Morgan fingerprint with the existing generator (radius 2, 2048 bits, bit vectors). Hydrogens are then counted as neighbours, so the environments differ for CH3, CH2 and CH groups. The rest of the pipeline is unchanged: the tanimoto helper, the descriptor RBF kernel (descriptors still computed from the heavy-atom molecule), the 0.5/0.5 kernel mix, and the SVR settings with the rank-normalized target. Only the Morgan input graph changes.
backlog.title: Explicit-hydrogen Morgan fingerprint

backlog.spec: Swap SVR(kernel='precomputed') for sklearn.kernel_ridge.KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=...) on the exact same combined kernel and rank-transformed target, choosing alpha by a short inner 5-fold CV over {0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0, 3.0} scored by Spearman. KernelRidge has a closed-form solution, uses every training point (no epsilon tube discarding the middle of the distribution), and is deterministic and fast on 970 molecules. Rationale: with a rank-uniform target the epsilon=0.05 insensitive tube ignores roughly the central band of the response, which is exactly the region where Spearman accumulates most of its pairwise comparisons; ridge regression on ranks optimises squared rank error, a much closer surrogate to Spearman.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge instead of epsilon-insensitive SVR

memo: Helped: changing model family (LightGBM 0.5726, Tanimoto-kernel SVR 0.5491, from 0.6103 start), rank-normalizing the target (0.5310/0.5307, replicated), and above all averaging the Tanimoto kernel with an RDKit 2D descriptor RBF kernel (0.4830, incumbent). Did not help: FCFP (0.5877), MACCS (0.5421), stacking (0.5558), MLP ensemble (0.5500), descriptor-only ridge (0.5328), 60-descriptor subset (0.4973), autocorrelation descriptors (0.5057), RankSVM (0.5957), Laplacian solve (0.5716). Within noise (sd about 0.0070): scaffold weighting 0.4803, KernelRidge 0.4822, descriptor weighting 0.4824, extra kernels (0.4854-0.4860). Gobbi kernel (0.4680/0.4791) and ridge prior (0.4711/0.4728) were borderline gains that did not hold up on replication. Kernels look plateaued near 0.48. Next: tune SVR C, epsilon and descriptor gamma; try a GP; try quantile-transformed descriptors; maybe combine Gobbi with the ridge prior. Read train.py first, since many edits aborted by assuming a random forest or LightGBM. Replicate gains under 0.01.
